title: Cancellation Fee Add-Back on Counted Add-On Refunds
content:
## Cancellation fee add-back — Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda overpayment recoveries

**Rule.** When the overpaid part of a paid GAP balance line is worked out, a product's cancellation fee may be added to the counted refunds. Two products count: a Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans plan and a Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts contract, each financed on the waiver's purchase deal.

Each add-on's reason is read from its completed cancellation request. An add-on counts only where both of these hold:
- it was cancelled on or after the loss date on the waiver's most recent paid GAP balance line, for the reason customer request or vehicle sold or traded; and
- its refund was paid to the lienholder.

The fee added is that product's own cancellation fee, as its own tier states it.

### Truth table

| Plan so cancelled, refund paid to the lienholder | Contract so cancelled, refund paid to the lienholder | Added to the counted refunds |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | the plan's cancellation fee plus the contract's cancellation fee |
| Yes | No | the plan's cancellation fee |
| No | Yes | the contract's cancellation fee |
| No | No | nothing |

An add-on counts as "No" in any of these cases: it was cancelled before the loss date; it was cancelled for the reason total loss or deal unwound; or no refund of it was paid to the lienholder.

### Cases (hypothetical)

- The plan was cancelled after the loss for customer request with its refund paid to the lienholder. The contract was cancelled after the loss for total loss. Only the plan's fee is added.
- Both were cancelled after the loss for vehicle sold or traded, with both refunds paid to the lienholder. Both fees are added.
- The plan was cancelled after the loss for customer request, but its refund came to 0.00 and nothing was paid to the lienholder. Its fee is not added.
